lines.shooter3d.help.move: {key:up}{key:left}{key:down}{key:right} MOVE  {key:sprint} SPRINT  {key:jump} JUMP, VAULT, MANTLE  {key:crouch} CROUCH, SLIDE
lines.shooter3d.help.fight: {key:fire} FIRE  {key:aim} AIM  {key:reload} RELOAD  {key:swap} SWAP  {key:melee} PUNCH  {key:grenade} GRENADE  {key:use} USE  {key:view} 1ST/3RD
lines.shooter3d.boot.land: The badlands: land, roads and outposts

notes.shooter3d.outpost.drop: An outpost's name (shown top left when the player is there, and on a banner when it is cleared): where the player is dropped in, with a firing range.
notes.shooter3d.outpost.relay: An outpost: a radio relay station with a tall mast.
notes.shooter3d.outpost.salvage: An outpost: a scrapyard of shipping containers.
notes.shooter3d.outpost.pump: An outpost: a water pump house with a water tower.
notes.shooter3d.outpost.ridge: An outpost: a camp of tents on a ridge.
notes.shooter3d.place.badlands: Where the player is when at no outpost (top left): the open, dry, rocky country between them.
notes.shooter3d.weapon.rifle: The rifle's name: Ranger is its model, AR short for assault rifle. Shown small under the ammo count.
notes.shooter3d.weapon.shotgun: The shotgun's name: a model name (it breaches doors). Shown small under the ammo count.
notes.shooter3d.loot.cell: A battery that recharges the player's energy shield.
notes.shooter3d.loot.syringe: A medical syringe that restores health.
notes.shooter3d.feed.pickup: The feed (top right): {item} picked up (one of the loot lines).
notes.shooter3d.feed.target_down: The feed (top right): a practice dummy at the firing range knocked down.
notes.shooter3d.feed.raider_down: The feed (top right): a raider killed.
notes.shooter3d.feed.heavy_down: The feed (top right): a heavily armoured raider killed.
notes.shooter3d.note.first_person: The camera now sees through the player's eyes.
notes.shooter3d.note.third_person: The camera now looks over the player's shoulder.
notes.shooter3d.banner.cleared: A banner when an outpost is taken: {outpost} is its name (one of the outpost lines).
notes.shooter3d.banner.progress: Under that banner: how many outposts of the {total} are cleared now.
notes.shooter3d.over.lost: The game over screen, after the player dies: raiders killed, then outposts cleared of {total}. Scoreboard labels each followed by its number, separated by three spaces.
notes.shooter3d.over.won: The title of the screen after winning: every outpost is cleared.
notes.shooter3d.over.kills: On the win screen: how many raiders were killed (a scoreboard label, then the number).
notes.shooter3d.over.time: On the win screen: how long the run took, {time} as minutes:seconds (4:07).
notes.shooter3d.use.zipline: A prompt by a zipline: {key:use} is the key or button that rides it.
notes.shooter3d.use.bin: A prompt by a supply crate: {key:use} opens it (ammo and health pop out).
notes.shooter3d.use.open_door: A prompt at a door: {key:use} swings it open, {key:melee} kicks it off its hinges. Two parts separated by three spaces.
notes.shooter3d.use.close_door: A prompt at an open door: {key:use} shuts it, {key:melee} kicks it off its hinges. Two parts separated by three spaces.
notes.shooter3d.compass.n: A compass point (north) on the compass at the top of the screen: one or two letters.
notes.shooter3d.compass.metres: The distance to an outpost, under its mark on the compass: {metres} the number, M short for metres. Keep it very short.
notes.shooter3d.hud.grenades: Beside the health bar: G short for grenades, {grenades} how many the player carries (0 to 4). Keep it very short.
notes.shooter3d.hud.slot: Small, above the gun's name: {slot} is the gun's slot (1 or 2), {weapon} the other gun's name (a weapon line).
notes.shooter3d.hud.outposts: Top right: the outposts cleared of the {total}.
notes.shooter3d.hud.left: Top left, at an outpost: how many raiders still hold it. (The English shows the plural for one as well.)
notes.shooter3d.hud.cleared: Top left, at an outpost no raider holds any more.
notes.shooter3d.hud.range: Top left, at the drop point: its firing range, with practice dummies to shoot.
notes.shooter3d.help.move: The controls, shown for the first seconds: each {key:...} is a key, then what it does, parts separated by two spaces ({key:up}{key:left}{key:down}{key:right} is WASD). VAULT: jump over low cover; MANTLE: pull up onto a ledge; SLIDE: crouch at a sprint.
notes.shooter3d.help.fight: The controls, second row: each {key:...} is a key, then what it does, parts separated by two spaces. PUNCH: the melee key; 1ST/3RD: switch between first and third person.
notes.shooter3d.help.mouse: Click the game to lock the mouse to it (it then turns the view).
notes.shooter3d.touch.use: A touch button's label: keep it to a few letters.
notes.shooter3d.touch.melee: A touch button's label (a punch): keep it to a few letters.
notes.shooter3d.touch.crouch: A touch button's label (crouch): keep it to a few letters.
notes.shooter3d.touch.kick: The punch button's label at a door (kick it in): keep it to a few letters.
notes.shooter3d.boot.land: A step on the loading screen: making the land, its roads and outposts.
notes.shooter3d.boot.world: A step on the loading screen: building the 3D world.
notes.action.aim: Aim down the gun's sights (the controls screen).
notes.action.melee: A punch, or a kick at a door (the controls screen).
notes.action.swap: Switch between the two guns (the controls screen).
notes.action.view: Switch between first and third person (the controls screen).

brief: The 3D shooter: open badlands (dry golden grass, red rock mesas) with six outposts; raiders, armed bandits with energy shields, hold five of them, and the player clears them with a rifle, a shotgun, grenades and fists, in first or third person. Its words are a shooter's HUD: terse, in capitals, in the corners of a 320 x 240 screen, so keep them short. The player character is an unnamed soldier, never said to be a man or a woman, and never addressed by name.
